No perpetual-duration language is included. The possibility of paid-up licensing is not demonstrably absent, so the conditional requirement cannot be treated as inapplicable.
The clause does not state that any paid-up licence is irrevocable. The possibility of paid-up licensing is not demonstrably absent.

elements.element: Subscription licences may be terminated only for material breach.
elements.evidence: No language restricts termination of subscription licences to material breach, and the existence of subscription licensing is not demonstrably excluded.

elements.element: A subscription licence may be terminated for material breach only if that breach remains uncured.
elements.evidence: The redline contains neither a cure right nor an uncured-breach trigger for termination.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to Customer's successors.
elements.evidence: Transfer is permitted only to a successor in connection with specified merger, amalgamation, reorganization, or business/asset-sale transactions. This does not provide the preferred unqualified transferability to successors.

elements.element: The licence extends to Customer's affiliates.
elements.evidence: Affiliated companies are expressly and automatically included in the licence grant.

elements.element: Customer's written notice is sufficient to extend affiliate coverage, without requiring consent.
elements.evidence: Affiliate coverage is automatic and requires neither notice nor consent, which is more permissive than coverage upon written notice.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction.
elements.evidence: Section 20(d) permits assignment without consent, together with the licence, to a successor in connection with a merger, amalgamation, reorganization, or sale of all or substantially all relevant assets or business.

result.reason: The redline reaches the fallback by providing automatic affiliate coverage and consent-free transfer to an M&A successor, and it also adds contractor coverage. It does not address perpetual or irrevocable paid-up licences or restrict subscription termination to uncured material breach, and its successor-transfer right is transaction-limited. It is not minimal because it unnecessarily grants the same expanded assignment right to Garman, altering the supplier's previously restricted assignment rights. Drafting is also internally awkward: the grant remains expressly “non-transferable” without a direct cross-reference to the later exception, and the bilateral proviso purports to let either party assign the agreement “together with the licence granted,” even though the licence is granted only to Sparkling.
